questions.question: 1. In the context of cell design, what is a primary consequence of *increasing* the pathloss exponent?

answers.a: The signal strength at the boundary increases.
answers.b: The signal strength at the boundary decreases.
answers.c: The effect of shadowing is eliminated.
answers.d: The cell coverage becomes more circular.

questions.question: 2. A 'log-normal' distribution is used to model shadowing because...

answers.a: signal strength is always a positive value.
answers.b: the random variations are measured in decibels, which is a logarithmic scale.
answers.d: it only applies to indoor environments.

questions.question: 3. If a cell is designed for 90% boundary coverage probability, what does this mean?

answers.a: 90% of the cell area has perfect signal.
answers.b: A user at the cell edge will have an acceptable signal 90% of the time or at 90% of locations.
answers.c: The data speed will be at 90% of its maximum.
answers.d: Only 10% of users can connect at the boundary.

questions.question: 4. What is the 'sensitivity level' or 'threshold' (gamma) used in coverage calculations?

answers.a: The maximum power the base station can transmit.
answers.b: The average power received by all users.
answers.c: The minimum signal strength required for acceptable service quality.
answers.d: The amount of interference from other cells.

questions.question: 5. How does a *larger* fade margin impact boundary coverage probability?

answers.c: It has no effect on the probability.
answers.d: It makes the signal quality worse.

answers.a: Lower than the boundary coverage probability.
answers.b: Higher than the boundary coverage probability.
answers.c: Exactly the same as the boundary coverage probability.

questions.question: 7. If two locations are at the same distance from a base station, why might they have different signal strengths?

answers.a: Due to different pathloss exponents at each location.
answers.b: Due to different levels of shadow fading from local obstacles.
answers.c: Because the base station transmits at different power levels.
answers.d: This is not possible; they must have the same signal strength.

questions.question: 8. What is the main purpose of calculating the pathloss exponent and shadow fading variance from measurements?

answers.a: To create statistical models that can predict large-scale propagation.
answers.b: To determine the exact speed of the radio waves.
answers.c: To choose the frequency for the base station.
answers.d: To count the number of obstacles in the area.

questions.question: 9. A 'circular coverage region' is defined by a radius where the...?

answers.a: signal is perfect and never drops.
answers.c: mean signal level is above a threshold with a certain probability.

questions.question: 10. If the standard deviation (sigma) of shadowing is zero, what would this imply?

answers.a: The signal strength is perfectly predictable by the pathloss model alone.
answers.b: There is no signal at all.
answers.c: The cell has an infinite radius.
